name: Electric science factory · 30/min each
setupNotes: Feed iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone, water and crude oil at the six labeled west-side ports.
The four science output chests are on the east edge.

Each input has an item/fluid display directly above its belt or pipe. Connect from the left; both belt lanes take the shown material. Press Alt to see the labels. Display panels need Circuit network research: leave their ghosts unbuilt until then; production works without the signs.
All smelting uses electric furnaces and electricity is external; no solid-fuel plant or furnace fuel route is included.
Fast transport belts, fast underground belts and fast splitters are used; no robots, modules, beacons or quality are included.
Smelt the raw ores and stone at the west end. Production runs on both sides of the bus, with direct feeds into the nearby machine rows. Each intermediate route ends after its last consumer.
Intermediate assemblers use a shared circuit clock to limit excess production during startup.
changes: Two production banks around a compact central bus; raw smelting is placed before the workshops.
Feeder belts enter from the bus-facing end of each machine row, eliminating long return loops.
One additional iron furnace and a higher gear-production limit keep all four science outputs at or above 30/min in the simultaneous benchmark.

name: Steel science factory · 30/min each
setupNotes: Feed iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone, water and crude oil at the six labeled west-side ports.
The four science output chests are on the east edge.

Each input has an item/fluid display directly above its belt or pipe. Connect from the left; both belt lanes take the shown material. Press Alt to see the labels. Display panels need Circuit network research: leave their ghosts unbuilt until then; production works without the signs.
Steel furnaces consume internally produced solid fuel from the light-oil branch; coal is reserved for grenades and plastic.
Fast transport belts, fast underground belts and fast splitters are used; no robots, modules, beacons or quality are included.
Keep the saved circuit wires and two clock combinators connected to balance intermediates and furnace fuel.
changes: Pure item recipes use deterministic compact blocks and one eastbound bus per material.
Steel furnaces replace electric furnaces and the oil adapter solid-fuel output is routed to every steel-furnace block.
Added seven solid-fuel branch-head stock gates; each reader is wired to a passive nearby red belt.
Added one read-only mixed-input line reader per steel-fuel block and bounded circuit relays so gates include shared-lane fuel stock.
Removed 21 unused furnace input tail belts and sized fuel branch reserves above trapped head stock.
